Contributions at a glance Exact stochastic results linking replication inside a cell, infection establishment and species diversification. 01 When does bursting help? Chapter 6 Chapter 8 At matched mean lifetime output, one dimensionless parameter L determines how bursting compares with continuous budding. Linear clearance Bursting lowers extinction risk exactly when L > 1 (when establishment is possible). Finite immune budget Bursting leaves more surviving output exactly when L < 1 (one delivery; positive integer budget). The extinction-probability gap is exact; at L = 1, the full offspring distributions coincide. Thm 6.8 / Prop 6.9 / Prop 8.12 02 An exact solution for two interacting types Chapter 7 For two types with one-way conversion, each type can trigger a catastrophe that ends the whole process. Two closed forms give the probability of avoiding catastrophe up to any time and the joint generating function of both counts before catastrophe . Thm 7.4 / Eq. 7.50 03 One bursting cell Chapters 4 and 5 Expresses load moments using one no-catastrophe probability and tracks release at finite time. Derives burst timing, explains why the burst-size and quasi-stationary laws agree, and extends the calculation to several founders and successive cell-to-cell transfers. 04 From cells to infection Chapter 6 An age-structured infection model with survival and release kernels derived from the cell process. It shows why fitted constant rates depend on the growth phase, and why one exponential phase cannot identify all three intracellular rates. 05 A branching constant explained Chapter 3 Kolmogorov’s survival constant A ( p ) is linked to the logistic map’s Koenigs function. A hypertranscendence proof rules out an elementary formula for that function in its spatial argument; the closed-form question for A ( p ) remains open. 06 Evolution under changing rates Chapter 9 A speciation model driven by unused population capacity yields an explicit limiting species-count distribution and variance. A moving critical point is derived for the Pimentel resistance model, locating reversals of competitive advantage. What is new? The originality index singles out four statements: the extinction-gap identity, coincidence of offspring laws, two-type no-catastrophe probability and joint generating function. These and the extensions above build on established methods. Full claims, sources and scope: Originality of the results , p. 270 . 3
